```{python}
#| label: convergence-setup
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
import plotly.express as px
from live_results import *

RUN_ROOT = source_path("refine-logs/convergence_10e/runs")
QUEUE_DB = source_path("refine-logs/convergence_10e/queue.sqlite")
runs = load_summary_tree("refine-logs/convergence_10e/runs")
completed = runs.query("run_state == 'completed'").copy()
partial = runs.query("run_state != 'completed'").copy()
metric_cols = numeric_metrics(completed)
queue = read_sql(QUEUE_DB, "select id, ordinal, status, attempts, completed_at, error from jobs order by ordinal")
```

## Why this is separate from screening

The original factorial queue used short screening runs. This chapter contains
only the promoted longer-budget extensions. A 3-, 10-, and 15-epoch result for
the same named architecture are different estimands because training budget and
checkpoint selection changed. The longest result supersedes the shorter result
for final ranking, but the shorter trajectory remains useful for diagnosing
whether screening preserved the ordering.

## Source and completion evidence

```{python}
#| label: convergence-provenance
display(source_inventory({"convergence queue": QUEUE_DB}))
display(queue.status.value_counts(dropna=False).rename_axis("queue_status").reset_index(name="jobs"))
display(runs.groupby(["run_state", "expected_epochs", "observed_lead"], dropna=False)
        .size().rename("runs").reset_index())
display(partial[[c for c in ["run_name", "expected_epochs", "epochs_completed",
                              "observed_lead", "summary_updated"] if c in partial]])
```

A summary file is marked completed only when its `_SUCCESS.json` exists or its
recorded completed epoch reaches the epoch count encoded in the run name.
Partial summaries are displayed for monitoring but excluded from leaderboards.

::: {.callout-warning}
The queue ledger is stale: it still labels 12 entries pending, whereas the run
tree contains 33 completed summaries (23 at 10 epochs and 10 at 15 epochs).
Completion and metrics here therefore come from terminal summaries and
`_SUCCESS.json`; the queue database is retained only as provenance.

## Complete validation, delineation, training, and resource metrics

```{python}
#| label: convergence-all-metrics
identity = [c for c in ["run_name", "observed_lead", "expected_epochs",
                         "best_epoch", "epochs_completed", "summary_updated"] if c in completed]
display(completed[identity + metric_cols]
        .sort_values(["expected_epochs", "observed_lead", "run_name"]))
display(pd.DataFrame({"metric": metric_cols,
                      "direction": [metric_direction(x) or "context only" for x in metric_cols],
                      "nonmissing_rows": [int(completed[x].notna().sum()) for x in metric_cols]}))
```

## Metric-specific leaders and Pareto view

```{python}
#| label: convergence-leaders
display(leaderboard(completed, metric_cols, id_col="run_name",
                    group_cols=("expected_epochs", "observed_lead"), k=TOP_K))
if {"val_recon_loss", "miou_wave", "peak_gpu_memory_bytes"}.issubset(completed):
    fig = px.scatter(completed, x="val_recon_loss", y="miou_wave",
                     color="observed_lead", symbol="expected_epochs",
                     size="peak_gpu_memory_bytes", hover_name="run_name",
                     hover_data=[c for c in ["val_missing_pearson",
                                             "val_missing_pearson_p05",
                                             "boundary_f1_smoke"] if c in completed],
                     title="Reconstruction–delineation–memory trade-off")
    fig.show()
```

The composite checkpoint score is
`mIoU + 0.25 × boundary F1 + 0.1 × Pearson`. Consequently, a retained
checkpoint can differ from the epoch with the best reconstruction correlation.
Any paper table must report that selection rule rather than implying that each
individual endpoint was independently optimized.

## Horizon-matched learning-budget effects

```{python}
#| label: convergence-horizon-matched
completed["configuration"] = (completed.run_name
    .str.replace(r"^conv(?:10|15)e_", "", regex=True)
    .str.replace(r"_s\d+_l[01]$", "", regex=True))
horizon_metrics = [c for c in ["val_missing_pearson", "val_missing_pearson_p05",
                                "val_recon_loss", "miou_wave", "boundary_f1_smoke",
                                "P_iou", "QRS_iou", "T_iou"] if c in completed]
wide = completed.pivot_table(index=["configuration", "observed_lead"],
                             columns="expected_epochs", values=horizon_metrics)
matched_horizons = wide.dropna().copy()
for metric in horizon_metrics:
    if (metric, 10) in matched_horizons and (metric, 15) in matched_horizons:
        matched_horizons[(metric, "15−10 improvement")] = (
            (matched_horizons[(metric, 15)] - matched_horizons[(metric, 10)]) *
            (-1 if metric_direction(metric) == "min" else 1))
display(matched_horizons.reset_index())
```

Across the five configurations completed at both horizons and both leads, the
extra five epochs consistently improve mean Pearson, reconstruction loss, wave
mIoU, and boundary F1. The gain is not a uniform shift: QRS IoU is already near
saturation and typically increases by only 0.0025–0.0075, whereas P/T IoU and
boundary F1 improve much more. Short screening therefore underestimates
slow-learning atrial and repolarization morphology.

The largest boundary-F1 gains occur for raw A0 (+0.089 lead I, +0.097 lead II),
showing that an apparently weaker short-run baseline can recover substantially
with budget. Three- or ten-epoch rankings cannot be presented as pure
architecture effects.

## Matched 15-epoch contrasts

```{python}
#| label: convergence-15e-contrasts
fifteen = completed.query("expected_epochs == 15").copy()
baseline = fifteen.query("run_name.str.contains('A0_raw')", engine="python")
keys = ["observed_lead"]
compare_metrics = [c for c in ["best_score", "val_missing_pearson",
                                "val_missing_pearson_p05", "val_recon_loss",
                                "P_iou", "QRS_iou", "T_iou", "macro_f1_wave",
                                "miou_wave", "boundary_f1_smoke",
                                "boundary_ppv_smoke", "boundary_sensitivity_smoke",
                                "peak_gpu_memory_bytes"] if c in fifteen]
base = baseline[keys + compare_metrics].rename(columns={m: f"base.{m}" for m in compare_metrics})
joined = fifteen.merge(base, on=keys, how="left")
for metric in compare_metrics:
    sign = -1 if metric_direction(metric) == "min" else 1
    joined[f"improvement.{metric}"] = sign * (joined[metric] - joined[f"base.{metric}"])
display(joined[["run_name", "observed_lead", *compare_metrics,
                *[f"improvement.{m}" for m in compare_metrics]]])
```

At 15 epochs, no configuration dominates every endpoint. On lead I,
`A0_wave_noSSL` has the highest mean Pearson (0.7474) and best reconstruction
loss (0.8377), while `R7` has the best boundary F1 (0.8784) and T/QRS overlap.
On lead II, physiology-informed `R5` leads mean Pearson (0.7607), lower-tail
Pearson (0.4304), mIoU (0.8627), macro F1 (0.9261), and boundary F1 (0.8886),
but `A0_wave_noSSL` retains the best reconstruction loss (0.7625).

This is encouraging for R5 on lead II but is not a clean SSL win. The principal
contrast `A0 raw → A0+wavelet → A0+wavelet+SSL` is incomplete because a matched
15-epoch A0+wavelet+SSL cell is absent. R5 changes the second view and training
objective, so it cannot identify whether wavelets, SSL, or UEG phase caused the
result. `C1_E1` remains a complementarity control; it does not support treating
E1 as an improved base architecture.

Until multiple seeds and external evaluation land, differences on the order of
one or two thousandths are treated as ties rather than mechanistic proof.

## Evidence ledger

| Question | Current answer | Why |
|---|---|---|
| Does longer training matter? | Yes, descriptively | All ten matched lead/configuration cells improve on major reconstruction and delineation endpoints from 10 to 15 epochs. |
| Is R5 the best completed model? | Endpoint- and lead-dependent | Strongest broad lead-II profile; not best lead-I reconstruction and not universally best loss. |
| Does UEG phase beat Morlet phase? | Suggestive on lead II, unresolved | R5 exceeds C1_E1 on several metrics, but the comparison also crosses A0/E1 architecture and lacks repeated seeds. |
| Does SSL add value beyond a wavelet branch? | Not yet identified | The matched 15-epoch A0+wavelet+SSL cell is missing. |
| Can validation select a clinical model? | No | Single seed, composite checkpoint selection, internal validation, and no paired per-record uncertainty. |
